    Crockpot Banana Oatmeal With Whole Bananas

    Published: Oct 12, 2026 by Megan Porta, comfort food recipe creator and founder of Pip and Ebby, known for easy family meals and Instant Pot desserts. · This post may contain affiliate links.

    Jump to Recipe
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 10:36
    Instaread

    This crockpot banana oatmeal starts with whole peeled bananas, so you can skip slicing or mashing them before cooking. Steel-cut oats, brown sugar and warm spices cook alongside the bananas overnight. In the morning, mash everything together for a bowl of banana bread oatmeal with breakfast already mostly handled.

    After making my overnight apple oatmeal with whole apples, of course I had to try bananas next! My thinking was the same: if I’m going to mash the fruit into the oatmeal anyway, why do that work before cooking?

    I left the bananas whole, sprinkled the brown sugar and spices over them and let the crockpot take over. Seven hours on low gave me creamy oatmeal and bananas I could mash right into the pot with a potato masher.

    Expect soft, spoonable oatmeal with banana throughout, rather than a sliceable baked oatmeal. I cook it with water and add milk or cream at the end so I can adjust the consistency after the bananas are mashed in.

    Why This Recipe Works

    • The bananas go in whole. Peel them and lay them over the oats. Save the mashing for the morning, when they’re soft enough to break apart easily.
    • Breakfast cooks overnight. Seven hours on low worked perfectly in my test, with just mashing, stirring and toppings left to do.
    • You get banana bread flavors in an oatmeal bowl. Ripe bananas, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and vanilla bring that familiar combination to breakfast.
    • You control the final texture. Mash thoroughly for banana throughout or leave a few soft pieces, then add milk or cream to loosen the oatmeal.

    Ingredient Notes

    Steel-cut oats: Use regular steel-cut oats for the version I tested. Rolled oats, quick oats and quick-cooking steel-cut oats are not direct substitutes for this timing and liquid ratio.

    Bananas: Use 3 to 4 ripe bananas, peeled and left whole. Ripe bananas provide more sweetness than underripe ones. They will soften and get mashed into the oatmeal, so they don’t need to hold their shape.

    Water: Four cups of water provide the cooking liquid for one cup of steel-cut oats. Milk or cream goes in after cooking.

    Brown sugar: Start with 1/4 cup packed brown sugar. You can add a little more near the end of cooking or adjust the sweetness when serving.

    Cinnamon and nutmeg: These give the oatmeal its warm banana bread flavor. The small amount of nutmeg complements the cinnamon without taking over.

    Salted butter and salt: Butter adds richness, while salt balances the sweetness.

    Vanilla extract: Stir this in after cooking.

    Milk or cream: Add a little at a time after mashing the bananas until the oatmeal reaches the consistency you like.

    Equipment You’ll Need

    • Crockpot or slow cooker: For cooking the oats and whole bananas overnight on low.
    • Potato masher: I use this to mash the softened bananas directly into the oatmeal after cooking. No transferring to another bowl! A fork or sturdy spoon also works.

    How to Make Crockpot Banana Oatmeal

    1. Prepare the crockpot. Coat the inside with nonstick cooking spray. Add the steel-cut oats and water, then stir briefly to combine.
    1. Add the whole bananas. Peel the bananas and lay them over the oatmeal mixture. There’s no need to slice or mash them first.
    1. Add the sugar, spices and butter. Combine the brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt in a small bowl. Sprinkle evenly over the bananas, then distribute the butter pieces over the top.
    1. Cook overnight. Cover and cook on low for approximately 7 hours, until the oats are tender and the bananas mash easily. If desired, sprinkle a little extra brown sugar over the bananas during the final 10 to 15 minutes and replace the lid.
    1. Mash and stir. Use a potato masher to mash the bananas directly into the oatmeal. A fork or sturdy spoon also works. Stir in the vanilla, then add milk or cream as needed.
    1. Finish your bowls. Spoon into bowls and add granola, chopped nuts, maple syrup or fresh banana slices.

    Recipe Tips

    • Seven hours is the timing I tested. Slow cookers vary, so check for tender oats and watch for dry edges the first time you make it. If yours tends to run hot, make the first batch during the day so you can check it.
    • Use low heat. This method is built around a long, gentle cook. I haven’t tested a shorter cook on high.
    • Mash before adding more liquid. Incorporate the bananas and stir everything together before deciding how much milk or cream you need.
    • The extra brown sugar is optional. You don’t need to interrupt your morning to add it before cooking finishes. Taste and adjust the sweetness when serving instead.
    • Expect the oatmeal to thicken as it sits. Add a splash of milk, cream or water to loosen it.

    Toppings and Serving Ideas

    • Banana bread bowls: Add chopped pecans or walnuts and a splash of cream.
    • A crunchy finish: Sprinkle granola or prepared cinnamon streusel over individual servings.
    • Fresh banana topping: Add sliced bananas just before serving.
    • Extra sweetness: Finish with a drizzle of maple syrup or a sprinkle of brown sugar.
    • Peanut butter banana oatmeal: Stir a spoonful of peanut butter into your bowl after cooking.

    How to Store and Reheat

    Refrigerator: Divide leftovers into shallow containers and refrigerate within two hours. Store covered for 3 to 4 days.

    Freezer: Freeze in individual portions in freezer-safe containers for up to 3 months for best quality.

    Reheating: Thaw frozen portions overnight in the refrigerator. Reheat in the microwave or a saucepan, stirring occasionally and adding a splash of water or milk to loosen the oatmeal. Heat leftovers to 165°F.

    Frequently Asked Questions

    Do I need to mash the bananas before cooking?

    No! This version starts with whole peeled bananas. They soften during cooking, then you mash them directly into the oatmeal before serving.

    Can I use rolled oats instead of steel-cut oats?

    Stick with regular steel-cut oats for this recipe. I tested the seven-hour cooking time and four cups of water with steel-cut oats. Rolled oats would need a different cooking time and potentially a different amount of liquid.

    Can I cook banana oatmeal longer than seven hours?

    Seven hours produced perfectly creamy oatmeal in my test. It may tolerate a little longer, but that depends on your slow cooker. Check the edges for dryness rather than assuming it can cook all night regardless of how long you sleep.

    Can I use milk instead of water?

    The version I tested uses water during cooking, with milk or cream added afterward. That’s the method I recommend for this recipe.

    Why did my banana oatmeal get so thick?

    Oatmeal thickens as it sits and cools. Mash the bananas, stir well and add milk, cream or water a little at a time to loosen it.

    Crockpot Banana Oatmeal With Whole Bananas

    Whole bananas cook overnight with steel-cut oats, brown sugar and warm spices. Mash them into the oatmeal in the morning for banana bread flavor without slicing or mashing before cooking.

    Print Pin Rate
    Course: Breakfast
    Cuisine: American
    Prep Time: 5 minutes minutes
    Cook Time: 7 hours hours
    Total Time: 7 hours hours 5 minutes minutes
    Servings: 6
    Calories: 227kcal
    Author: Megan Porta

    Equipment

    • Slow Cooker
    • Potato masher

    Ingredients

    • 1 cup steel-cut oats
    • 4 cups water
    • 3-4 ripe bananas peeled and left whole
    • 1/4 cup brown sugar plus more for finishing if desired
    • 1 tsp ground cinnamon
    • 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
    • 1/2 tsp salt
    • 2 Tbsp salted butter cut into 3-4 pieces
    • 1 tsp vanilla extract
    • Milk or cream for serving

    Optional Toppings

    • Granola or cinnamon streusel
    • Chopped pecans or walnuts
    • Maple syrup
    • Fresh banana slices

    Instructions

    • Coat the inside of a Crockpot with nonstick cooking spray.
    • Add the steel-cut oats and water directly to the Crockpot. Stir briefly to combine.
      1 cup steel-cut oats, 4 cups water
    • Lay the whole peeled bananas over the oatmeal mixture.
      3-4 ripe bananas
    • In a small bowl, combine the brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt. Sprinkle the mixture evenly over the bananas.
      1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg, 1/2 tsp salt
    • Distribute the butter pieces over the tops of the bananas.
      2 Tbsp salted butter
    • Cover and cook on Low for 7 hours.
    • During the final 10 to 15 minutes, sprinkle a little additional brown sugar over the bananas, if desired. Replace the lid and finish cooking.
      1/4 cup brown sugar
    • Use a potato masher to mash the softened bananas directly into the oatmeal. A fork or sturdy spoon will also work.
    • Stir in the vanilla. Add milk or cream until the oatmeal reaches your preferred consistency.
      1 tsp vanilla extract, Milk or cream
    • Spoon into bowls and add your favorite toppings.
      Granola or cinnamon streusel, Chopped pecans or walnuts, Maple syrup, Fresh banana slices

    Notes

    • Use regular steel-cut oats. This cooking time and liquid ratio were tested with regular steel-cut oats, not rolled, instant or quick-cooking varieties.
    • Choose ripe bananas for the sweetest flavor. Peel them, but leave them whole before cooking.
    • Slow cookers vary. Seven hours on low produced creamy oatmeal in my test. Check for tender oats and dry edges the first time you make it.
    • Mash to your preference. Mash thoroughly for banana throughout or leave a few soft pieces for texture.
    • Adjust after mashing. Stir in the vanilla, then add milk or cream a little at a time. The oatmeal thickens as it sits.
    • Extra brown sugar is optional. Sprinkle it over the bananas during the final 10 to 15 minutes, or adjust the sweetness when serving.
    • Store leftovers covered in the refrigerator for 3 to 4 days. Reheat with a splash of milk or water to loosen.
      Mash the bananas and stir everything together before adding milk or cream. The oatmeal thickens as it sits, so adjust the consistency just before serving.
